name: Posaconazole
mechanism: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent 14α-lanosterol demethylase, blocking ergosterol synthesis → disrupts fungal cell membrane integrity. Broad spectrum: Candida, Aspergillus, Mucorales (Zygomycetes), Fusarium, Scedosporium. Fungistatic (fungicidal at high concentrations)
dosing: Prophylaxis (neutropenia/GvHD): Oral suspension 200mg TDS with food OR gastro-resistant tablet 300mg BD day 1, then 300mg OD OR IV 300mg BD day 1, then 300mg OD. Treatment (invasive infection): Loading 300mg BD day 1, then 300mg OD (oral tablet/IV). Use gastro-resistant tablet or IV (NOT suspension) for treatment - more reliable levels. Take tablet with food. IV: infuse over 90 min via central line (vesicant). Therapeutic drug monitoring: target trough >0.7mg/L (prophylaxis), >1mg/L (treatment)
contraindications: Coadministration with CYP3A4 substrates that prolong QT (pimozide, quinidine, halofantrine) or ergot alkaloids (ergotism). Hypersensitivity to azoles. Caution: QT prolongation risk, electrolyte disturbances, hepatic impairment
interactions: EXTENSIVE CYP3A4 interactions - potent inhibitor. AVOID: simvastatin, lovastatin, atorvastatin (rhabdomyolysis), ergot alkaloids, pimozide, quinidine (arrhythmias), ritonavir/efavirenz (complex bidirectional), rifampicin/rifabutin (antagonism, ↓ posaconazole levels). CAUTION: ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus (↑ levels - reduce dose 25-50%, monitor levels), warfarin (↑ INR), vinca alkaloids (neurotoxicity), midazolam, digoxin, phenytoin (complex). PPIs, H2RAs, metoclopramide ↓ absorption (suspension only - use tablet/IV if needed, or separate by hours)
monitoring: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) - trough levels at steady-state (day 7-10). Target: >0.7mg/L (prophylaxis), >1mg/L (treatment), ideally 1-3mg/L. LFTs baseline and weekly initially, then monthly (hepatotoxicity). Electrolytes (K, Mg, Ca) - correct before starting (QT risk). ECG if cardiac risk factors (QT prolongation). Renal function. FBC. Signs of infusion reaction (IV). Clinical response (fever, inflammatory markers)
pregnancy: AVOID unless life-threatening infection with no alternative. Teratogenic in animals (skeletal abnormalities). No adequate human data. Contraception advised during treatment. Consider alternatives (liposomal amphotericin if systemic infection needed in pregnancy)
sideEffects: Common: GI upset (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain), headache, rash, fever. Hepatotoxicity (transaminase elevation, rarely severe - monitor LFTs). QT prolongation (especially if electrolyte imbalance, concurrent QT drugs). Hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia. IV: infusion reactions (phlebitis - central line required). Uncommon: Stevens-Johnson syndrome/TEN (rare), adrenal insufficiency (high-dose, prolonged), pancreatitis, haemolytic uraemic syndrome (rare)
pharmacokinetics: Oral suspension: variable absorption, requires food (preferably fatty meal) and gastric acid. Bioavailability ~30-50%. Tablet (gastro-resistant): more consistent absorption, not affected by pH, higher bioavailability (~70%). IV: 100% bioavailability. Highly protein-bound (>98%). Not significantly metabolized (mostly excreted unchanged). Half-life: 20-35h. Steady-state 7-10 days. Excreted: 77% faeces (unchanged), 14% urine (glucuronide metabolites). TDM essential (wide inter-patient variability)
clinicalPearls: Brand: Noxafil. BROAD-SPECTRUM azole - covers Aspergillus, Candida, Mucorales (Zygomycetes), Fusarium, Scedosporium. UNIQUE: only azole with reliable Mucorales activity (mucormycosis/zygomycosis - alternative to amphotericin). USES: prophylaxis in high-risk neutropenia (AML/MDS chemotherapy, allogeneic HSCT with GvHD), treatment of invasive aspergillosis (refractory/intolerant to voriconazole/amphotericin), treatment of mucormycosis. FORMULATIONS: oral suspension (variable absorption - requires food, avoid if possible), gastro-resistant tablet (preferred oral - reliable absorption), IV (central line required - vesicant). For TREATMENT, use tablet or IV (not suspension - unreliable levels). THERAPEUTIC DRUG MONITORING: essential due to variable pharmacokinetics. Target trough >0.7mg/L (prophylaxis), >1mg/L (treatment). Check at day 7-10, then periodically. Adjust dose if subtherapeutic (double dose if needed). INTERACTIONS: extensive CYP3A4 inhibitor - reduce calcineurin inhibitor doses (ciclosporin, tacrolimus) by 25-50%, monitor levels. Avoid statins (rhabdomyolysis). PPI/H2RA: only affects suspension (not tablet/IV). QT PROLONGATION: correct electrolytes before starting, ECG if risk factors. MUCORMYCOSIS: posaconazole alternative to amphotericin (better tolerated, oral option). Often used as salvage or step-down after initial amphotericin. Better tolerated than voriconazole (less visual disturbance, photosensitivity). More expensive than fluconazole/itraconazole. IV preparation: sulphobutyl ether β-cyclodextrin (SBECD) vehicle - accumulates in renal impairment (use oral if CrCl <50). RESISTANCE: emerging in Aspergillus (cross-resistance with other azoles - cyp51A mutations). Consider combination therapy or amphotericin if resistance suspected. PROPHYLAXIS: highly effective in preventing invasive fungal infections in high-risk haematology patients (superior to fluconazole/itraconazole). Duration: throughout neutropenia and GvHD immunosuppression
indication: Prophylaxis of invasive fungal infections in high-risk patients (neutropenia from AML/MDS chemotherapy, allogeneic HSCT with GvHD). Treatment of invasive aspergillosis (refractory/intolerant to amphotericin or voriconazole). Treatment of mucormycosis (zygomycosis). Treatment of chromoblastomycosis, mycetoma, coccidioidomycosis (refractory)
